title: Support desk copilot
tagline: Give every agent an AI assistant that drafts replies and summarizes long ticket threads — without a single customer name, order number, or complaint ever leaving the building.
scenario: An upset customer emails about a damaged delivery. An agent pastes the thread into the assistant and gets a warm, on-brand reply in seconds — apology, replacement offer, next steps. What used to take ten minutes of careful wording takes one.
steps: The button below opens Chat with a real support scenario ready to send.
Hit Send and watch the reply stream — and the GPU meter climb.
Follow up conversationally: “make it shorter”, “offer a discount instead”.

ctas.label: Run it live in Chat →
ctas.prompt: A customer emailed: 'This is the second time my order arrived damaged. Order #48231, a docking station. I need it for work Monday and I'm honestly fed up.' Draft a short, empathetic reply that apologizes, offers an overnight replacement, and keeps their business.

why.head: Private by default
why.body: customer PII stays on a machine you own, not in a cloud provider's logs.

why.head: No per-seat AI fees
why.body: one device serves the whole support team, flat cost.

why.head: Always on
why.body: no internet outage can take the assistant down mid-shift.

notes: Point at the telemetry strip while the reply streams — “that's the answer being computed, in this room.”
If they ask about their own helpdesk: any tool that can call an API can call this box (Ollama speaks the standard OpenAI-style API).
